profile.reading:
This building, TX21, is located at 5207 Rogers Road in the Westover Hills area of San Antonio, TX (one secondary source, DataCenterHawk, instead places it at nearby 3800 Wiseman Boulevard within the same Westover Hills parcel; the two addresses are not fully reconciled across sources, so this discrepancy is flagged rather than resolved). Vantage does not publish this campus on its own site at all, so this entry relies on secondary sourcing: Data Center Dynamics reporting on the building permit. TX21 covers approximately 360,000 square feet across three stories, at a stated construction cost of roughly $157 million; its permit was originally filed for a December 2023 to June 2025 timeline, but the launch date appears to have slipped and is unclear as of this research. No power/MW figure is disclosed in any source found, and no certifications are published, consistent with the building's incomplete status.

Vantage acquired 31 acres at State Highway 151/Wiseman Boulevard in August 2023 for its Westover Hills sub-campus, home to TX21 and TX22, separate from the Texas Research Park sub-campus (Omicron Drive, home to TX11 and TX12). This San Antonio campus is distinct from Vantage's much larger "Frontier" mega-campus, a separate $25 billion, 1.4-gigawatt, 3.7-million-square-foot, 1,200-acre development in rural Shackelford County, Texas, announced in August 2025 to meet AI demand.

San Antonio's data center growth, including Vantage's TX cluster, has concentrated on the city's West and Northwest sides where CPS Energy, the nation's largest municipally owned combined electric and gas utility, has courted large industrial and data center loads with dedicated substations and negotiated rate agreements. Bexar County and the City of San Antonio have both offered Chapter 313-successor and local property-tax abatement agreements to data center developers as part of broader economic-diversification efforts beyond the city's traditional military and tourism base. CPS Energy's long-range integrated resource planning has specifically flagged data centers as a fast-growing large-load category requiring new generation and transmission investment through the early 2030s, a dynamic Texas's ERCOT grid operator has also cited statewide as it revises long-term demand forecasts upward.

reading.body:
Vantage Data Centers TX21 is a 360,000-square-foot building under construction in San Antonio's Westover Hills district on a 31-acre campus acquired in August 2023. The operator has not published any power capacity, cooling, or certification details for this facility, so its technical specifications remain opaque. Secondary sources report a construction cost near $157 million and a timeline that appears to have slipped past its original June 2025 target, leaving launch timing unclear.

A claimed 32 megawatts of IT capacity would support roughly 800 racks at a typical 40 kW per-rack AI training density, though no operator statement confirms this power figure. The absence of any published specifications on Vantage's website indicates the campus remains in development and not yet operational. This facility represents one of 133 mapped data center locations in Texas but ranks nineteenth among the eighteen facilities in the state with published power capacity, meaning most of the state's mapped capacity comes from other operators.

San Antonio's municipal utility, CPS Energy, has systematically developed infrastructure and negotiated rate agreements to attract large data center loads on the city's west side, and both city and county have offered tax abatement under state incentives. CPS Energy's own integrated resource planning explicitly flags data centers as a driver of new generation and transmission requirements through the early 2030s. This context explains the presence of multiple Vantage buildings in the region, though Vantage's announced $25 billion Frontier mega-campus in rural Shackelford County, rather than San Antonio, signals where the operator expects its largest Texas AI demand to concentrate.
